display.title: The Real Color of Geulah
display.summary_short: Why the reward of the World to Come cannot be described, explained through the Rambam's clever test of a 'cured' blind man, with a story about the power of bentching from a siddur.
display.summary_long: The storyteller starts with the Yehi Ratzon said after the daily Nasi, which speaks of a light that 'no eye has seen' except Hashem. Not everything that exists can be seen, like a smell, sound, wind or electricity, and the Mishnah teaches that one moment of the World to Come, when this world becomes better than Gan Eden in the days of Moshiach, is worth more than all the pleasures of this life. To show that holy words carry hidden power, he tells of a young scholar who asked the Rebbe whether to take a job in Eretz Yisroel for parnassah; the Rebbe told him that the words and letters of Birkas HaMazon, read from a siddur, bring parnassah. Then comes the story of the Rambam, chief doctor to the sultan. Jealous doctors claim they can cure a man born blind, and at the royal trial the man counts fingers. But when the Rambam holds up red and blue cloths and he names the colors, the Rambam shows they are fakers, since someone who has never seen cannot know the names of colors. So too, the Sages cannot describe the reward of the Geulah, because nothing in our world compares to it.
display.lesson: Holy words of davening and brachos carry great hidden power, and the reward waiting for us with Moshiach is beyond anything we can imagine.
